issue: उदय केत सम हित सब ही के: हित read as the welfare that the comet's rising strikes at, or as ironic 'for the good of all' in the mock-praise of the wicked.
our reading: Their rise, like Ketu's, harms the welfare of all (हित = welfare, which the comet's rising bodes ill for).
alternatives: Literal ironic praise: their rise is like Ketu's, 'for the good of all' (the irony carrying the sense of harm).

issue: सदा may go with करउ … उर धाम (always dwell in my heart) or with छीरसागर सयन (who ever lies on the ocean of milk).
our reading: May he who rests on the ocean of milk make my heart his home for ever (सदा with the prayer).
alternatives: Gita Press: सदा with शयन — who always lies on the ocean of milk, may he dwell in my heart.

issue: Subject of जो सहि दुख परछिद्र दुरावा: cotton (in the image, covering others' holes as cloth) or the saint (covering others' faults).
our reading: Cotton, with the pun glossed: it covers others' holes (faults); the line describes cotton and through it the saint.
alternatives: The saint as subject directly (Gita Press Hindi), or cotton only (Gita Press English).

issue: Whom धींग धरमध्वज धंधक धोरी describes: the poet (मोरी … धोरी, "I, a brazen hypocrite, foremost in schemes") or the whole group of cheats of 12.cau1–2a.
our reading: It describes the poet: after 'among them my count is first', the line names what he is (a brazen rogue who flies the flag of dharma, foremost in worldly schemes).
alternatives: The four words are further attributes of the group (those who are brazen, hypocrites, bearers of schemes), among whom the poet is counted first; the sense of the verse is the same either way.

issue: Who is settled where: लोक बिसोक बनाइ बसाए after सिय निंदक अघ ओघ नसाए; the subject is understood from प्रभुहि in the line before.
our reading: The Lord destroyed the sins of Sītā's slanderer and made the townspeople free of sorrow and settled them in his own realm (लोक = his abode).
alternatives: Gita Press English reads the townsfolk as the subject, damned by the slanderers' sins yet lodged in a heavenly abode; others read बिसोक लोक as 'a sorrowless world' without 'his own'.

issue: जपि जेईं पिय संग भवानी: जेईं (from जेवना/जीमना, to dine) against a reading 'keeps repeating it with her husband'.
our reading: Bhavānī repeated the Name and dined with her husband (the story of the thousand names equalled by one Rāma-nāma).
alternatives: Gita Press Hindi: पार्वतीजी सदा अपने पतिके साथ रामनामका जप करती रहती हैं; Gita Press English agrees with ours (dined).

issue: प्रीति परसपर प्रभु अनुगामी: which of name and named is the master and which the follower is left open by the words.
our reading: Their mutual love is that of a master and the one who follows him, without saying which is which.
alternatives: Gita Press: the named (the Lord) follows the Name, as a servant follows his master; some read the name as following the named.

issue: Parse of 'जग प्रिय हरि हरि हर प्रिय आपू': each word read once (Hari is dear to the world; Nārada himself is dear to Hari and Hara), or with an added clause 'Hara is dear to Hari' as Gita Press brackets.
our reading: The world holds Hari dear, and Nārada himself is dear to Hari and to Hara.
alternatives: Hari is dear to the world, Hara is dear to Hari, and Nārada is dear to both (Gita Press, with the middle clause in brackets).

issue: रामकथा कलि पंनग भरनी: भरनी as 'peahen' is not in Monier-Williams, Apte or Platts (they give the nakshatra Bharaṇī, a weft or shuttle, and in MW a plant, Luffa foetida or similar).
our reading: a peahen (मोरनी) to the serpent of the Kali age, the usual reading and our glossary's
alternatives: a herb (bharaṇī) that counters the serpent of Kali, as a plant against snake venom

issue: सुकृती साधु नाम गुन गाना: whose singing, of what? Either the singing of the virtues of the virtuous, of the saints and of the Name (the book's praises of saints and of the Name), or the singing of the Name and virtues done by virtuous saints.
our reading: songs in praise of the virtuous, of the saints and of the Name (पुण्यात्माओं, साधुओं और नामके गुणोंका गान)
alternatives: the singing of the Lord's Name and virtues by virtuous saints

issue: जेहि दिन राम जनम श्रुति गावहिं: do the Vedas sing that this day is Rāma's birth, or do they sing (declare) that all the tīrthas come there on that day?
our reading: on the day the Vedas celebrate as Śrī Rāma's birth, all the tīrthas come there
alternatives: the Vedas say that on the day of Śrī Rāma's birth all the tīrthas come there

review: Disagree with leaving it open: the context (Satī took Sītā's form in this body; she is reborn as Pārvatī and weds Śiva) settles एहिं तन as Satī's present body. Applied in the hi/en fixes above; remove the doubt.
Agree with the writer's reading (Satī's self-description, in apposition to मैं; fairer and grammatical, style.md §2); settle it and remove the doubt.
Agree: जाति अवमाना as dishonour among one's own kin fits the line and MW jāti (family, lineage); settle and remove.
reviewer_fix: settled: dishonour among one's own kin

issue: कौतुकहीं गिरि गेह सिधाए: Nārada went playfully (for his own delight) or out of eager curiosity at the news
our reading: Hindi कौतुकवश ही (holds both); English 'playfully', as the review set it
alternatives: out of curiosity, eagerly (MW kautuka 'curiosity, interest, eagerness'), English 'went eagerly / out of curiosity'

issue: नारि सहज जड़ अग्य: Satī's description of herself (in apposition to मैं) or a general statement about women that she makes
our reading: Satī's self-reproach: I, a woman dull and unknowing by nature, deceived Śambhu (the words stand beside मैं in the same line)
alternatives: A general statement in Satī's mouth: a woman is by nature dull and unknowing (Gita Press)

issue: जाति अवमाना: whose dishonour — dishonour suffered among / at the hands of one's own kin, or an insult offered to one's kin (here her husband)
our reading: dishonour among one's own kin (स्वजनोंके बीच होनेवाला अपमान): Satī is slighted in her father's house and Śiva is slighted there
alternatives: the insult offered to one's own people (Gita Press English)
जाति-अपमान left unglossed (Gita Press Hindi)

issue: एहिं तन: whose body — Satī's present body (in which she took Sītā's form) or Śiva's
our reading: left as the verse has it: in this body there shall be no union between Satī and me
alternatives: Satī's present body (Gita Press: सतीके इस शरीरसे; the reading the story bears out, as she is reborn as Pārvatī)

issue: Nārada's 'गूढ़' words list the groom's 'faults' in words that also read as virtues of Śiva: अगुन (without merit / beyond the guṇas, nirguṇa), अमान (without honour / free from pride), मातु पितु हीना (without parents / unborn), उदासीन (indifferent / detached), संसय छीना (heedless / free of doubt). Which surface to give in the meaning?
our reading: The words as the parents hear them, kept neutral where Hindi allows both senses: गुणोंसे रहित, मानसे रहित / without qualities, without honour; the verse itself calls them अवगुन, and 69.cau2 says Nārada saw these 'faults' in Śiva.
alternatives: Gita Press Hindi: गुणहीन, मानहीन; Gita Press English: 'devoid of merits, free from pride' (one sense each). A reading that gives the hidden sense (beyond the guṇas, free from pride) would anticipate 69.cau2.

issue: Whether सकल लोक अभिराम (delight of all the worlds) qualifies Śiva or Hari.
our reading: Hari, the noun it follows (Gita Press reads it so too).
alternatives: Śiva, the subject of the dohā, as delight of all the worlds.

issue: दूरि करेहु संदेहु: whose doubt is to be cleared is not named — Pārvatī's, or that of Himavān and the household about her resolve.
our reading: सन्देह दूर करो / clear away the doubt (left unnamed, as in the verse)
alternatives: उनका (पार्वतीजीका) सन्देह दूर करो / dispel her doubts (Gita Press); dispel Himavān's doubt

review: Agree with the writer: जोगि जमात beside प्रेत and पिशाच is the band of yoginīs (the same train is listed with जोगिनि at bal.95.cha1); settle it as written and drop the doubt.
reviewer_fix: Keep the meaning as written (योगिनियोंके झुंड / bands of yoginīs); remove the doubt.

review: Agree with the writer: सही read as 'true' (the boon that follows is a prophecy that holds) fits the line and the next dohā; settle it and drop the doubt.
reviewer_fix: Keep सच्चे वचन बोले / spoke these true words; remove the doubt.

issue: जोगि जमात: जोगि may be read as योगी (ascetics) or, as a short form, योगिनी (the yoginīs of Śiva's train).
our reading: योगिनियोंकी जमातें / bands of yoginīs, as in the same list at bal.95.cha1 (जोगिनि) beside प्रेत and पिशाच.
alternatives: जोगियोंकी जमातें / bands of yogis (ascetics).

issue: बोले सही: सही taken as 'true, sure' (words that will come true); it may also be a rhyme-filler meaning 'indeed'.
our reading: सच्चे वचन बोले / spoke these true words (the boon that follows is a prophecy that holds).
alternatives: सचमुच बोले / indeed spoke; Gita Press: सुन्दर (सान्त्वना देनेवाले) वचन.

review: Agree: the verse names no one whose offences are to be forgiven, and the neutral 'सब अपराध' / 'every offence' is the plain reading of the words; settle it as written and drop the doubt.
Agree: the subject runs on from महतारी in the line before, and Mainā has already bowed at Pārvatī's feet knowing her as Jagadambā (bal.99.cau1); keep the mother as subject and drop the doubt.

issue: सुभग सुमंगल गावहिं नारी: सुभग may qualify नारी (fortunate, i.e. married women) or the songs with सुमंगल (beautiful, auspicious songs); Monier-Williams gives both 'very fortunate … dear (as a wife)' and 'beautiful, lovely'.
our reading: सुभग with नारी: सुहागिन स्त्रियाँ सुन्दर मंगलगीत गाने लगीं / wedded women sang beautiful auspicious songs (सुन्दर / beautiful from the सु- of सुमंगल).
alternatives: सुभग with the songs: स्त्रियाँ सुन्दर, शुभ मंगलगीत गाने लगीं / the women sang lovely, auspicious songs.

issue: सुमिरि गिरापति प्रभु धनुपानी: गिरापति 'lord of speech' is in Monier-Williams a name of Bṛhaspati (gir-īśa, gīṣ-pati, vāk-pati); here it may be an epithet of the bow-bearing Lord or a separate figure.
our reading: One person: the Lord Śrī Rāma, master of speech, bow in hand (the next caupāī, bal.105.cau3, makes Rāma the puppeteer of Sarasvatī, i.e. the lord of speech).
alternatives: Two remembered: गिरापति as Brahmā (Sarasvatī's lord) or Bṛhaspati, and then the Lord with the bow.

issue: पुनि पुनि मिलति परति गहि चरना: the verse names no subject and no owner of the feet; the previous line's subject is the mother (महतारी), the next line's is Bhavānī.
our reading: The mother (Mainā) embraces Umā again and again and falls clasping her feet (Mainā knows her as the Mother of the world, cf. bal.99.cau1 पुनि पुनि पारबती पद बंदे).
alternatives: Umā embraces her mother again and again and falls at her mother's feet, as a daughter would at a farewell.

issue: छमेहु सकल अपराध: whose offences — the verse names no one.
our reading: Left open as the verse has it: forgive every offence (Hindi सब अपराध क्षमा कीजियेगा).
alternatives: Umā's offences (Mainā asks Śiva to bear with her daughter as his household servant); Mainā's own offences (her harsh words about Śiva and Nārada in bal.96–97).

review: Agree with the writer: नाग here is the elephant and its foe the lion, so 'lion's skin' is the plain reading of the words (MW's nāgāri, Garuḍa, cannot fit a skin); the tiger skin is the usual picture, not what the words say. Keep our reading; settle the doubt so.

Agree with the writer: परमानंद अमित सुख पावा reads plainly as the object (he attained supreme bliss, boundless joy); taking परमानंद as Śiva's epithet supplies a subject the line does not need. Keep our reading.
reviewer_fix: उन्होंने परमानन्द तथा अपार सुख पाया / he knew supreme bliss, a joy beyond measure

issue: नागरिपु छाला: नाग here is the elephant, and the elephant's foe is the lion (our word meaning; MW has nāgāri only as Garuḍa, the serpents' foe); Śiva's seat is commonly pictured as a tiger skin.
our reading: सिंहकी खाल / a lion's skin
alternatives: बाघम्बर / tiger skin (Gita Press, by the usual image of Śiva)

issue: परमानंद अमित सुख पावा: परमानंद may be the object with अमित सुख (he attained supreme bliss and boundless joy) or an epithet of Śiva as subject (Śiva, himself supreme bliss, attained boundless joy).
our reading: उन्होंने परमानन्द तथा अपार सुख पाया / he knew supreme bliss, a joy beyond measure
alternatives: स्वयं परमानन्दस्वरूप शिवजीने भी अपार सुख पाया / Śiva, the embodiment of supreme bliss, found boundless joy (Gita Press)

issue: बिनु बानी बकता बड़ जोगी: whether जोगी is योगी (yogī) or योग्य (able, skilled), qualifying बकता.
our reading: बिना वाणीके ही वक्ता हैं; वे महान् योगी हैं / without speech he speaks: he is the great yogī (Platts and our word sheet give जोगी only as योगी)
alternatives: बिना वाणीके बड़े योग्य वक्ता हैं / a most skilful speaker without speech (Gita Press, reading जोगी as योग्य)

review: Agree with the writer: निगूढ़ is 'hidden, secret, obscure' (MW, Apte); the Lord's words (133.cau1, the physician withholding harmful food) were indeed veiled. Keep our reading; the doubt can be settled and removed.
reviewer_fix: श्रीहरिकी गूढ़ वाणीको समझ न सके / did not grasp the hidden sense of Śrī Hari's words

issue: समुझी नहिं हरि गिरा निगूढ़ा: निगूढ़ा is 'hidden, secret, obscure' (Monier-Williams, Apte, ni-gūḍha), so the line says Nārada did not grasp the hidden sense of Hari's words (the physician who withholds harmful food). Gita Press reads it as अगूढ़ (स्पष्ट), 'even such plain words'.
our reading: श्रीहरिकी गूढ़ वाणीको समझ न सके / did not grasp the hidden sense of Śrī Hari's words
alternatives: भगवान्‌की अगूढ़ (स्पष्ट) वाणीको भी न समझ सके / could not understand even such unambiguous words (Gita Press)

review: agree: बिसमय beside हरष is dismay (विषाद), as in our ayodhya.12.cau2 (बिसमय हरष रहित → न विषाद … न हर्ष); settled, apply and drop from the doubts file

issue: बिसमय paired with हरष: wonder (विस्मय) or dismay/grief (विषाद)?
our reading: dismay (विषाद): neither grieving nor rejoicing over making the good bad and the bad good; Tulasī's बिसमय often has this sense beside हरष
alternatives: wonder, surprise (Skt vismaya, MW/Apte): neither surprise nor joy

review: Agree: both easy and hard, so it cannot be told; cau2's second line and Gita Press bear it out. Settle as written.
Agree: address 'friend of devotees', parallel to अनाथ हित (bal.146.cau2); settle as written.
Agree: MW viśva-vāsa 'the receptacle of all things' confirms 'in whom the universe dwells'; settle as written.

issue: सुगम अगम कहि जाति सो नाहीं: whether the longing is both easy and hard and therefore cannot be told, or whether one cannot say if it is easy or hard.
our reading: It is both easy and hard, and it cannot be put into words (the next line: easy for the Lord to give, hard for Manu to ask; in cau4 Manu leaves it to the Lord who knows it).
alternatives: It cannot be said whether it is easy or hard to obtain.

issue: भगत हित: an address to the Lord (friend of devotees) or 'for the good of devotees' (the boldness pleases him for his devotees' sake).
our reading: Address: 'O friend of your devotees', as with अनाथ हित in bal.146.cau2.
alternatives: Even though, for the good of devotees, such boldness pleases you.

issue: बिस्वबास: 'in whom the universe dwells' (MW viśva-vāsa, receptacle of all things) or 'who dwells in all the universe'.
our reading: In whom the whole universe dwells (सम्पूर्ण विश्वके निवासस्थान), following Monier-Williams.
alternatives: Who dwells in (pervades) the whole universe.

review: सब बिधि कुसल कुबेष बनाएँ is open and not in the doubts file: कुसल as 'skilful' (ours: able in every way, yet in a lowly guise) or as 'well, safe' (MW kuśala: well, prosperous; Gita Press: in a poor guise lies welfare of every kind), which the next line's तेहि तें (that is why the destitute are dear to Hari) suits.
reviewer_fix: {"id": "bal.161.cau1", "issue": "सब बिधि कुसल कुबेष बनाएँ: कुसल can be 'skilful, able' (MW, Apte) or 'well, safe, prosperous' (MW); the line is either 'though able in every way, they wear a lowly guise' or 'in a lowly guise it is well with them in every way'; the next line's तेहि तें suits either.", "our reading": "सब तरहसे कुशल होकर भी वे दीन-हीन वेश बनाये रहते हैं / able in every way, they go about in a lowly guise", "alternatives": "दीन-हीन वेश बनाये रहनेमें ही उनका सब प्रकारसे कल्याण है / in a lowly guise it is well with them in every way (Gita Press)"}

issue: समुझि राजसुख दुखित अराती: whose royal happiness the enemy broods on is not stated — Pratāpabhānu's present royal joys (envy, which the smouldering kiln-fire image suits) or his own lost kingdom (Gita Press: अपने राज्य-सुखको समझ करके).
our reading: राजसुखकी बात सोच-सोचकर वह शत्रु दुखी था / Brooding on the joys of royalty, that enemy was in pain (left open, as the verse leaves it)
alternatives: अपने (खोये हुए) राज्यसुखको याद करके / remembering his own lost royal happiness (Gita Press); राजाके राजसुखको देखकर / at the sight of the king's royal happiness

issue: हाँकि न होइ निबाहु: हाँकि can be the king's shout of challenge to the boar (Platts hāṅk: call aloud, halloo; also driving onward), with न होइ निबाहु as what he cries (no escape now), or the driving of the horse; सुटुकि is taken as whipping (Platts suṭkun: switch, cane).
our reading: राजा घोड़ेको चाबुक लगाकर तेज़ीसे चल पड़ा और ललकारा कि अब तेरा बचाव नहीं होगा / touched his horse with the whip and sped towards it, crying out that now it had no escape
alternatives: hāṅki as urging the horse on, with न होइ निबाहु meaning the boar could not get away (narration, not the king's cry)

review: Agree with the writer: बिप्रहु is vocative plural (the voice addresses the Brahmins, who are present and hear it in the next line); the doubt can be settled and removed.

issue: बिप्रहु: vocative plural (हे ब्राह्मणो!) or बिप्र + हु 'the Brahmins too / even the Brahmins' (our word sheet)?
our reading: Vocative: the voice from the sky addresses the Brahmins — 'Brahmins, you gave the curse without thinking; the king has done no wrong.' -हु is Tulasīdāsa's vocative plural (भाइहु), the voice speaks to them, and 173.do has already said, in narration, that they gave it no thought.
alternatives: 'Even the Brahmins did not curse after due thought' (हु = भी), spoken of them in the third person.

review: Agree with the writer: Śiva is the speaker (184.cau2 addresses भवानी in the same passage); keep the single gloss (शिवजीने)/(Śiva). Doubt can be settled as written.

Agree with the writer: Monier-Williams gives durgama only as 'inaccessible' (noun 'a difficult situation'), not 'fortress'; the plain reading, a mountain made by Brahmā, very vast and hard to reach, stands. The fort (गढ़, 179.cau2) is what Maya built on it. Doubt can be settled as written.

issue: Who is मैं in मैं ब्रह्माँ मिलि तेहि बर दीन्हा: the narrator speaks in the first person in a passage that Yājñavalkya opened with मुनि सुनु.
our reading: Śiva (the narrator of the Mānas to Pārvatī) speaks: Brahmā and I together gave the boon; एवमस्तु … कीन्हा is the boon's words; marked once with a round-bracket gloss (शिवजीने / Śiva).
alternatives: Read एवमस्तु … कीन्हा as Brahmā's words alone and मैं as Yājñavalkya reporting Śiva's words without the gloss.

issue: बिधि निर्मित दुर्गम अति भारी: whether दुर्गम describes the mountain Trikūṭa (hard to reach) or stands as a noun, a fortress on it built by Brahmā, which Maya then refitted.
our reading: Trikūṭa, a mountain made by Brahmā, very vast and hard to reach; Maya adorned it anew with jewelled mansions of gold.
alternatives: A very great fortress built by Brahmā stood on Mount Trikūṭa, and Maya restored that fortress (Gita Press; गढ़ in bal.179.cau2 fits a fort).

review: Agree with the writer: no king is named in this or the nearby verses (the women, the bards), and ताहू ('he too') in the second half implies the givers also kept nothing back; सब काहू as the agent fits. Gita Press's English reads the same. Settle and apply as written.

Agree with the writer's reading (the king places the two shares in the hands of Kausalyā and Kaikeyī, so gladdening them, and gives them to Sumitrā); the grammar (हाथ धरि … मन प्रसन्न करि, both absolutives of the king's दीन्ह) supports it. Settle as written.

issue: सर्बस दान दीन्ह सब काहू: सब काहू can be the ergative subject (everyone gave) or the recipient (the king gave to everyone).
our reading: Everyone gave away all they had; those who received did not keep it either.
alternatives: The king gave his all to everyone (Gita Press Hindi: राजाने सब किसीको भरपूर दान दिया).

issue: कौसल्या कैकेई हाथ धरि … मन प्रसन्न करि: whose mind is gladdened, and what placing the shares in their hands means.
our reading: He placed the two parts in the hands of Kausalyā and Kaikeyī, so gladdening their hearts, and gave them to Sumitrā.
alternatives: He gave them to Sumitrā with a glad heart himself; or the two queens themselves handed the shares to Sumitrā.

review: Agree with the writer: narration is the plain reading (past तेहिं सुख माना, narration resumes in the next verse); the Hindi and English leave it readable either way, so no change.
Agree with the writer: हरि is a lion in Monier-Williams (a lion, MBh., Kāv.) and our word meaning; tiger is a custom-based reading, so lion stays.

issue: Whether the second line (मुनि धन जन सरबस सिव प्राना । बाल केलि रस तेहिं सुख माना) continues Vasiṣṭha's words to the king or is the narrator's.
our reading: Narration: the guru's speech is the first line's second half (बेद तत्व नृप तव सुत चारी); the second line, in the past tense (तेहिं सुख माना), tells of Śrī Rāma's delight in childhood play, and the next verses go on in narration.
alternatives: Gita Press takes it as the guru's words continued (of the four, Śrī Rāma, the sages' wealth …, has taken delight in childish play).

issue: हियँ हरि नख: the animal whose claw forms the child's amulet.
our reading: A lion's claw: हरि = lion (Monier-Williams, Apte; our word meaning gives सिंह).
alternatives: Gita Press: बाघके नख / tiger's claw, after the customary बघनखा amulet of children.

review: Agree: हित जानि 'knowing him as his well-wisher' with भगति adverbial is the plain reading (हित entry: हितैषी); keep as written and settle.
Agree with the eagerness reading (सह + रोष, the word entry 'with fervour'); the English must say the same (see the en item for line 0).

issue: अँबारी: our reading, with the word entry (छज्जे / अटारियाँ, balconies), is jewelled balconies over the bazaar; Platts gives अम्बारी (corr. of Arabic ʿamārī) as a canopy, a canopied litter on an elephant, which would make it canopies or awnings over the market.
our reading: विचित्र अटारियाँ, मणियोंसे जड़ी / wondrous balconies, studded with jewels
alternatives: विचित्र मणिमय शामियाने, चँदोवे (wondrous jewelled canopies or awnings over the bazaar)

issue: भगति हित जानि: whether भगति is adverbial (with devotion) and हित जानि 'knowing him as his well-wisher/friend', or भगति हित = 'for the sake of devotion' / 'one who loves devotion'.
our reading: Knowing the Lord to be his well-wisher, the sage served him bulbs, roots and fruit with devotion.
alternatives: Knowing that the Lord is fond of devotion (भक्तिका हितैषी), he served him food.
Knowing it to be for the sake of devotion (that the Lord accepts it), he served him food.

issue: सहरोसा: सह + रोष literally 'with passion/anger', which does not fit a gift; commentators take it as 'eagerly, gladly'.
our reading: बड़े उत्साहसे / gladly.
alternatives: सहर्ष, हर्षके साथ (with joy)
ज़ोर देकर (emphatically, insisting)

review: Agree with the writer: the line continues the first (इन्ह कै प्रीति परसपर), so the natural love likened to Brahman and the soul is the brothers' love for each other; our meaning ('यह … सहज स्नेह है' / 'it is a natural love') says so. Settle it and drop the doubt.
reviewer_fix: Keep the meaning as written; remove the doubt.

review: Agree with the writer: कंधर is the neck (MW kaṃ-dhara, the neck); 'necks like a lion's' is the plain reading. Settle it and drop the doubt.
reviewer_fix: Keep सिंहकी-सी गर्दन / necks like a lion's; remove the doubt.

issue: Whose love is 'ब्रह्म जीव इव सहज सनेहू' — the brothers' love for each other (continuing the first line), or Janaka's own natural love for Rāma, as the soul's for Brahman?
our reading: Left as the verse puts it: Janaka, delighted, says it is a natural love like that between Brahman and the soul; read with the first line, the brothers' mutual love.
alternatives: Some commentators take it as Janaka speaking of his own love for Rāma (he the jīva, Rāma Brahman).

issue: केहरि कंधर: कंधर is 'neck' in Monier-Williams and Apte; many renderings say lion-like shoulders.
our reading: Necks like a lion's (MW kaṃdhara, the neck).
alternatives: Shoulders like a lion's.

review: Agree: 'for the sake of devotion' is the plain sense of हेतु and fits the context (the Lord's wonder is a play for his devotees, as bal.225.cau4 says: he shows the power of worship). Settle and remove.
reviewer_fix: Keep: भक्तिके लिये / for the sake of devotion.

review: Agree: bal.230.cau3 (हृदयँ सराहत) and bal.230.do230 (सिय सोभा हियँ बरनि प्रभु) make the 'I' Śrī Rāma's inner praise; the plain first person is right. Settle and remove.

Agree with keeping it plain: the address सखी marks one friend's words to another, and naming a speaker would decide what the text leaves open; मोहि पाहीं in bal.233.cau3 reads naturally in either. Settle and remove.

issue: Whose is the 'I' in केहिं पटतरौं बिदेहकुमारी: Śrī Rāma praising Sītā in his heart (bal.230.do230: सिय सोभा हियँ बरनि प्रभु) or the poet speaking?
our reading: Kept as a plain first person ('to whom shall I compare'), which in context is Śrī Rāma's inner praise begun in bal.230.cau3.
alternatives: The poet Tulasīdāsa's own aside on Sītā's beauty.

issue: Who speaks in bal.233.cau3–cau4 (मुखछबि कहि न जाइ मोहि पाहीं; सावँर कुअँर सखी सुठि लोना): one of Sītā's friends describing the princes to another, or the poet addressing the reader?
our reading: Kept plain with no speaker named: 'I cannot tell … Friend, the dark prince … is lovely beyond measure', read as a friend's words.
alternatives: The poet's description, with सखी as a friend of Sītā addressed by the narrator.

issue: भगति हेतु: 'for the sake of devotion' (to honour his devotees' love, or to show what devotion does) or 'won over by devotion'?
our reading: for the sake of devotion / भक्तिके लिये
alternatives: because of (his devotees') devotion; conquered by devotion

issue: तव भुज बल महिमा उदघाटी । प्रगटी धनु बिघटन परिपाटी — two parallel statements (the sun has revealed the might of your arms; the way the bow will be broken has appeared), or one of purpose (the bow-breaking procedure has come about in order to reveal the might of your arms).
our reading: Two parallel statements, continuing the sun-image of the first half: उदघाटी (fem. past, agreeing with महिमा) and प्रगटी are both finite verbs; परिपाटी = order, method (MW pari-pāṭi: succession, order, method).
alternatives: Gita Press links them as purpose: the bow-breaking was set going in order to reveal the might of his arms.

review: Agree with the writer: रुख as 'facing', each saw Śrī Rāma turned towards himself; the next half-line (no one knew the secret) fits a marvel. Settle as written.
reviewer_fix: Keep the reading as written; remove the doubt.

review: Agree with the writer: line 1 continues the conviction of bal.245.cau1 (असि प्रतीति … और …); the speech opens at अस बिचारि गवनहु घर भाई. Settle as written.
reviewer_fix: Keep the reading as written; remove the doubt.

issue: रचेउ न धनु दमनीय: दमनीय is in Monier-Williams 'tamable, to be restrained' (a gerundive), and our word meaning is 'subduable'; does it describe the one Brahmā did not make (the one by whom the bow can be subdued), or the bow (Brahmā did not make the bow tamable)?
our reading: With पावनिहार: Brahmā seems not to have made the one who would win the princess, the victory and the fame, the one for whom the bow is subduable / धनुषको वशमें करनेवाला; the line laments that no such man exists, as bal.252.cau2-3 go on (बीर बिहीन मही).
alternatives: Brahmā did not make the bow such as could be subdued (दमनीय of धनु), with पावनिहार 'a winner' standing alone.

issue: निज निज रुख रामहि सबु देखा: रुख as 'facing' (each saw Śrī Rāma turned towards himself, the secret being this marvel) or as 'disposition' (each saw him according to his own feeling, as in bal.241)?
our reading: Each saw Śrī Rāma turned towards himself / हर किसीने श्रीरामजीको अपनी ही ओर मुँह किये देखा; the following कोउ न जान कछु मरमु बिसेषा fits a marvel no one understood.
alternatives: Each saw him according to his own inclination or feeling.

issue: Where the kings' speech begins: line 1 (बिनु भंजेहुँ … मेलिहि सीय राम उर माला) as the rest of the conviction in everyone's mind (bal.245.cau1), or as the first words spoken?
our reading: Line 1 continues the conviction ('and that even without the breaking …'); the speech opens with अस बिचारि गवनहु घर भाई, which the other kings answer in bal.245.cau3.
alternatives: Line 1 already spoken by the kings.

review: Agree with the writer: आजु लगें as 'until today' (as in bal.167.cau2 and the word sheet); GP's 'for this very day' is possible but not the plain reading.
Agree: the plain words (resolved on love with her body) without GP's bracketed gloss; the reading matches GP's sense.
Agree: ठाढ़ें describes Śrī Rāma standing (bow drawn), as GP also reads; the onlookers reading is weaker.
Agree: डोल as swing (हिंडोला), the moon's orb as the swing the fish play in.

issue: आजु लगें कीन्हिउँ तुअ सेवा: 'I have served you until today' or 'it was for today that I served you' (लगि as 'for the sake of')?
our reading: until today / आजतक, as आजु लगें in bal.167.cau2 (आजु लगें अरु जब तें भयऊँ) and the word sheet (लगें: तक).
alternatives: for this very day I served you (Gita Press: आजहीके लिये).

issue: प्रेम तन ठाना: what Sītā resolved 'with the body' (तन); the second तन as 'body', the first (प्रभु तन) as 'towards'.
our reading: she resolved on love with her very body / शरीरसे प्रेमका निश्चय ठान लिया (the plain words, with no gloss).
alternatives: she resolved that her body would be his or not live at all (Gita Press's bracketed gloss); she set her whole being on love.

issue: काहुँ न लखा देख सबु ठाढ़ें: whether ठाढ़ें describes Śrī Rāma ('all saw him standing', the bow already drawn) or the onlookers ('all stood watching').
our reading: No one saw him take it, string it or draw it; all saw only that he stood there.
alternatives: no one perceived it though all stood looking on.

issue: बिधु मंडल डोल: डोल as a swing (the moon's orb as the swing the fish play in) or as 'swaying' (the fish sway in the moon's orb).
our reading: as if Kāmadeva's two fish were at play in a swing that is the orb of the moon / चन्द्रमण्डलरूपी झूलेमें
alternatives: as if the two fish played, swaying, in the moon's orb.

issue: देखा राम नयन के भोरें: what did Śrī Rāma's eyes mistake the bow for?
our reading: Lakṣmaṇa sets it against जून धनु (an old bow): Śrī Rāma's eyes were deceived and took it for a new (sound) bow, so he handled it and it broke at a touch (272.cau2). Written: आँखोंके धोखेमें इसे नया समझकर / looked at it with eyes deceived, taking it for new.
alternatives: Rāma merely glanced at it by chance (भोरें = unwittingly), with no thought of new or old.

issue: रामु लखनु दसरथ के ढोटा: Viśvāmitra's words introducing the brothers, or the narrator's apposition?
our reading: Kept as plain apposition (seeing the fine pair, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, the sons of Daśaratha, he blessed them), adding no speaker the verse does not name.
alternatives: Viśvāmitra's introduction: These are Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, sons of Daśaratha.

issue: बाउ कृपा मूरति अनुकूला: what बाउ (wind) refers to and how मूरति is construed in Lakṣmaṇa's sarcasm.
our reading: The breeze (wind) of your grace befits your form; when you speak, flowers seem to fall (sarcastic: Paraśurāma's 'mercy' is as gentle as his person).
alternatives: कृपा मूरति as a vocative, 'O embodiment of mercy, the wind is favourable to you'; बाउ as the bodily humour vāta, a jibe that his 'mercy' is a fit of wind.

issue: राख in क्रोध भएँ तनु राख बिधाता: 'keep, protect' (राखै) or 'ashes' (pun).
our reading: When you are angry, may the Creator protect your body (राख = रखे, रक्षा करे).
alternatives: A pun on राख 'ashes': when angry, the Creator (alone knows / makes) the body ashes.

issue: हसि in सरुष हसि तहूँ बंधु सम बाम: 'laughing' (हँसि) or the Awadhi verb 'you are' (हसि = है).
our reading: Paraśurāma spoke angrily with a laugh: You too are as perverse as your brother (the verb 'are' understood).
alternatives: सरुष = angrily, हसि = 'you are': 'he said angrily: you are crooked like your brother'.

review: Agree: 'the bow of Ramāpati (Viṣṇu)' fits Vālmīki's Vaiṣṇava bow and the grammar; the vocative reading is the alternative. Settle as written.
Agree: MW sindhura = elephant, so सिंधुर मनि = gajamuktā; the vermilion reading is weaker. Settle as written (English wording fix above).

issue: राम रमापति कर धनु लेहू: कर as the genitive (the bow of Ramāpati) or as 'hand', with रमापति a vocative (Rāma, lord of Lakṣmī, take the bow in hand).
our reading: Rāma, take in your hand this bow of Viṣṇu, the lord of Lakṣmī, and draw it (the Vaiṣṇava bow Paraśurāma carries, as in Vālmīki).
alternatives: हे राम! हे लक्ष्मीपति! धनुषको हाथमें लीजिये — रमापति an address, कर = हाथ.

issue: सिंधुर मनिमय: सिंधुर as gajamuktā (pearls held to come from elephants' heads) or as sindūra, vermilion (red gems or vermilion-red squares).
our reading: The squares were made of gems of elephant-pearl (gajamuktā), naturally lovely.
alternatives: सिंधुर = सिंदूर: squares filled with vermilion and gems, or of vermilion-red gems.

review: Agree with the writer's reading (love delights in love; the literal sense of प्रीति कै प्रीति सुहाई, the same in hi and en). Gita Press English's 'love for the embodiment of love' is an addition.
Agree: गुर नारीं as the elders' wives (गुरुजनोंकी स्त्रियाँ) is the plain reading of गुर = elder and covers the guru's wife too.
Agree: दाता is an agent noun (giver), more naturally the gods than the flowers; the writer's reading stands.

issue: नागर नट: the city's dancers or skilled dancers
our reading: skilled dancers (चतुर नट): their expertise in rhythm is what makes their amazement at the horses' keeping time meaningful
alternatives: the dancers of the city (नगरके नट), Monier-Williams nāgara 'town-bred, civic'

issue: प्रीति कै प्रीति सुहाई: whose love, and how it relates to the decorating
our reading: yet love delights in love (प्रीतिको प्रीति ही सुहाती है), so auspicious adornments were made with care
alternatives: love upon love, i.e. the people's love overflowing, so the city was adorned (Gita Press: प्रीति-पर-प्रीति होनेसे); the people's love for Śrī Rāma, the embodiment of love (Gita Press English)

issue: गुर नारीं: the guru's wives or the elder women of the household
our reading: the elders' wives (गुरुजनोंकी स्त्रियाँ)
alternatives: the elderly women of the palace (बड़ी-बूढ़ी स्त्रियाँ); the wife of the guru Vasiṣṭha and other elders' wives

issue: सुमंगल दाता: qualifies the gods or the flowers
our reading: the gods, givers of every blessing, rain flowers
alternatives: they rain flowers that bring great blessing (Gita Press: सुन्दर मङ्गलदायक फूलोंकी वर्षा)

issue: मनहुँ सरोबर तकेउ पिआसे: who is the lake and who the thirsty? सरोबर (direct) with पिआसे (oblique) and the transitive perfect तकेउ can be read either way.
our reading: As if a lake had set out towards (set its eyes on) the thirsty: the lake is Viśvāmitra with the two brothers going to Daśaratha, who thirsts to see his sons (the striking reversal of the usual image); this follows the plain sense of चले, whose subject is the party that moves.
alternatives: As if the thirsty had set eyes on a lake: पिआसे as agent (प्यासेने), the thirsty being the brothers, whose longing (लालचु) to see their father is told in cau3, and the lake Daśaratha.

issue: ईस सम: whom does Janaka take Daśaratha to be equal to — the Lord (ईश्वर) in general, or Śiva (Maheśa)?
our reading: ईश्वरके समान / equal to God
alternatives: महादेव शिवजीके समान / the peer of Śiva (Gita Press)

issue: काम कोकिल लाजहीं: 'Kāmadeva's cuckoos are abashed' or 'Kāmadeva and the cuckoos are abashed'?
our reading: कामदेवकी कोयलें लजाती हैं / the cuckoos of Kāmadeva are put to shame (parallel to काम गज, 'the elephants of Kāmadeva', in bal.318.cau2)
alternatives: कामदेव और कोयलें लजाते हैं / Kāmadeva and the cuckoos are put to shame

issue: बारी: which service caste is meant — torchbearers or makers of leaf-plates (Platts gives both)?
our reading: Hindi बारी kept; English 'the bārīs (torchbearers and leaf-plate makers)'
alternatives: torchbearers (Gita Press English)
leaf-plate makers

issue: कलप सत सहस सारदा सेषु: 'a thousand Sarasvatīs and Śeṣas in a hundred kalpas' or 'hundreds of thousands of Sarasvatīs and Śeṣas in countless kalpas'?
our reading: a hundred kalpas; a thousand Sarasvatīs and a thousand Śeṣas
alternatives: लाखों सरस्वती और शेष लाखों कल्पोंमें (Gita Press's alternative)

review: Agree with the writer: सबहि carries over, the onlookers become पूरनकामा on seeing Śrī Rāma; the doubt can be settled as written.

Agree that the line is open and the writer's reading is the plain one; add as a further alternative that the joyful Brahmins (subject) have the guru, Gaurī and Gaṇeśa worshipped (गुरु-गौरी-गणेश as the usual triad). Keep the meaning as written.
Agree: बिलोकनि-बिरह (fear of losing the sight) is a natural reading of the words; Gita Press's 'arm and gaze' is the alternative. Keep as written.
Agree: सुरभी with long ī is the cow (as elsewhere in the Mānas); cow's ghee stands.

issue: Who is पूरनकामा in देखि राम भए पूरनकामा: all the onlookers on seeing Śrī Rāma, or Śrī Rāma on seeing Sītā?
our reading: सबहि carries over: seeing Śrī Rāma, all had every wish fulfilled (Gita Press Hindi reads the same).
alternatives: Śrī Rāma, seeing Sītā, had his heart's desire fulfilled (Gita Press English).

issue: गुर गौरि गनपति मुदित बिप्र पुजावहीं: are the Brahmins among those worshipped, or the agents of the worship?
our reading: The gurus have Gaurī, Gaṇeśa and the Brahmins worshipped.
alternatives: The gurus have Gaurī and Gaṇeśa worshipped through the Brahmins (Gita Press's bracketed alternative); or the gurus and Brahmins together have the worship done.

issue: बिलोकनि: object of चालति (she moves neither her arm nor her gaze) or part of बिलोकनि बिरह (separation from the sight)?
our reading: Jānakī does not move her arm, for fear of losing the sight of him (बिलोकनि-बिरह).
alternatives: She moves neither her creeper-like arm nor her gaze, for fear of separation (Gita Press).

issue: सुरभी सरपि: cow's ghee (सुरभी, f., cow) or fragrant ghee (सुरभि, adj., fragrant)?
our reading: cow's ghee (the feminine form सुरभी; our word meaning; Gita Press).
alternatives: fragrant ghee (MW and Apte: surabhi adj. sweet-smelling).

review: Agree with the writer: सुसारा read as fine goods in general (Platts su-sār; our word meaning); 'beds' is Gita Press's narrower reading and is not required by पठईं. Settle as written; no change.

issue: सुसारा in पठईं जनक अनेक सुसारा: goods and comforts in general, or beds (bedsteads) in particular?
our reading: many fine things (Platts: su-sār, substance, property, convenience, accommodation; MW su-sāra, good substance; our word meaning: comforts, furnishings).
alternatives: many fine beds (Gita Press, Hindi and English); the feminine plural पठईं would suit शय्या, but also वस्तुएँ.

issue: Who is रघुकुलमनि, the one who enters the city: Śrī Rāma or King Daśaratha?
our reading: King Daśaratha: the second line (सुमिरि … मुदित महीपति सहित समाजा) has no verb of its own and gives the subject of पुर प्रबेसु … कीन्हा, so रघुकुलमनि and महीपति are the same person.
alternatives: रघुकुलमनि is most often Śrī Rāma; then Śrī Rāma enters at the guru's word and the king follows gladly with his company (the verb supplied from the first line).

issue: What does तिहु लोक उजागर qualify: the glory (जसु) or the one whose glory is sung?
our reading: the glory renowned through the three worlds (उजागर = renowned, with जसु).
alternatives: Gita Press: the glory of Śrī Rāma, who illumines the three worlds (उजागर as the one who gives light to all).

review: Disagree with the writer's reading: बिलोकहु needs an object and the first half-line supplies it; the second line (सुंदर बधुन्ह सासु लै सोईं …) is narration. Settle as in the fixes above and drop the doubt.
reviewer_fix: Settled: the queens bid their friend look at the resplendent city and radiant night; the second line is narration.

issue: सुआसिनि (Skt. suvāsinī): Monier-Williams gives both 'a woman, married or single, who resides in her father's house' (the daughters and sisters of the house) and 'a respectable woman whose husband is alive'.
our reading: Married women whose husbands are alive (सुहागिन स्त्रियाँ), invited after the Brahmins' wives and given robes.
alternatives: The married daughters and sisters of the royal house living in their father's home.

issue: How far the queens' words (रानीं कहहिं बिलोकहु सजनी) run: whether the first half-line (पुरी बिराजति राजति रजनी) and the second line (सुंदर बधुन्ह सासु लै सोईं …) are inside the speech or narration.
our reading: The first half-line is narration placed before the speech, the speech is just 'Look, friend', and the second line is narration: the mothers-in-law went to sleep holding the brides, as serpents hide their crest-jewels in their breasts.
alternatives: The city and the night are what the queens bid their friends look at (Gita Press); or the second line too is spoken by the other queens of the palace about the three mothers.

issue: कबिकुल जीवनु पावन: whether पावन is a separate attribute of the glory (the life of the poets' race, and purifying) or governs जीवनु (purifying the life of the poets' race).
our reading: Śrī Rāma and Sītā's glory is the life of the poets' race, purifying, and a mine of blessings (three attributes in a row, as the line lists them).
alternatives: Gita Press Hindi: कविकुलके जीवनको पवित्र करनेवाला (it purifies the poets' life); its English gives both 'the very life and sanctifier'.
